author: The Exponent
title: Purdue baseball sets high hopes for Big Ten rebound - NewsBreak
text:
12 hours ago After narrowly missing out on qualifying for the tournament last year, Purdue baseball is entering the 2026 season with one goal in mind: Win the Big Ten Championship.
With the addition of 23 new players, Purdue enters the 2026 baseball season with a fresh start after last season’s disappointing results. Only five of the 14 position players that started at least 15 games last season will be returning, making it hard to predict how this season will go.
Much of the team is new to Division I baseball with 10 JUCO transfers and five freshmen. Head coach Greg Goff will turn to key returning leaders like junior right-handed pitcher Cole Van Assen, senior infielder and outfielder Aaron Manias, and fifth year infielder CJ Richmond to guide younger players.
Purdue begins the season at Constellation Field in Sugar Land, Texas. The stadium is home to the Sugar Land Space Cowboys, a Triple-A affiliate of the Houston Astros. This marks one of the three different Triple-A stadiums the Boilers will play at for the 2026 season, and the first time in program history that the team has played in three different minor league stadiums.
Rotation not set, CVA coined as staff ace
Van Assen stands as the only returning member from the 2025 season. He’s produced a 4.29 ERA in two seasons as a Boilermaker, including a rotation-best 4.28 ERA last year. He previously slotted behind starting pitchers Carter Doorn and Easton Storey, who have graduated and transferred, respectively.
For the team, Van Assen has his sights set on the conference championship. But for him personally, the goal is to build off of last season and “be the ace for the staff.”
Jackson Bessette, a senior catcher who recently transferred from the University of Illinois Chicago, expressed his admiration for the pitching staff, stating that Van Assen is “going to be that rock we’re looking for on a Friday night.”
The rest of the rotation behind Van Assen remains unclear. Goff previously cited left-handed pitcher Lucas Grant as one of his top recruits, but the freshman has dealt with an injury that may affect his ability to make an immediate impact on the mound.
“We have a pretty good idea. We just want to get through one more weekend and see exactly how we feel about them. But we’re close … with the rotation,” Goff said.
Bessette’s mindset for the upcoming games is sure to guide the team through its tough opponents, where the Boilers plan to face two ranked teams in their first eight games.
With fresh crop of position players, Goff looking for veterans to step up
A high-powered offense a year ago that scored 7.54 runs per game, ranking seventh in the conference, will have large shoes to fill following the departure of Second Team All-Big Ten junior infielder Logan Sutter, who led the team with a 1.180 OPS.
“I don’t know if you can ever replace those numbers. Logan was a great player for setting some records here, but it’s on to the next,” Goff said. “We’ve got a lot of guys. CJ Richmond was hurt a lot last year. We’re expecting a lot of big things from him, to be honest with you. Aaron Manias is the other guy. Both these guys will be hitting in the middle of the order.”
Bessette has come to Alexander Field for the past three years as a member of the visiting Flames. On March 15 last year, he delivered a two-home run performance against the Boiler pitching.
“I always had a lot of fun playing at (Alexander Field). It’s beautiful, the culture that they always had. I respected it. I wanted to be a part of that,” Bessette said.
While relying on the older players to step up, Goff also sees promise in the new players. He pointed out freshman infielder Westin Boyle, whom he sees having a great chance of being the team’s opening day shortstop, despite never having given that position to a freshman before.
The team hopes to improve upon many aspects of the game this season, anticipating redemption after falling short of making the tournament in 2025. As always, the goal is a Big Ten championship win, but the conference looks to be competitive with UCLA ranking No. 1 in preseason polls.
“(The) first step is just to flush it and learn from it,” Manias said on moving past the disappointment of last season. “This is my last year of college baseball, I’m just looking for whatever to make this team win.”
Rigorous schedule to present early-season tests
Last season saw the Boilers come out of the gate blazing hot with an 18-2 start, largely on the back of beating inferior opponents. Purdue did not face a ranked opponent until then-No. 24 UCLA on March 28, the Boilers’ 25th game of the season.
This season is projected to be a different story, with No. 20 Southern Missouri and No. 12 Oregon State coming up quick in Games 6 and 8 in the Round Rock Classic.
“We’ve got off to a really good start the last few years. And this year, we felt like we wanted to get off to a great start as well, but really jump the competition up a little bit,” Goff said. “And so when we got that invitation, we couldn’t turn it down.”
Purdue’s first eight games will be held in the warmth of Texas, and the team returns at 4 p.m. on March 6 to Alexander Field for its home opener against Oregon.
“We’re ready to make that next step and go in and have some type of a regional type environment so our guys can see that stuff. I think it’s going to be huge for us as we get ready for conference play,” Goff said. “We’re ready”.
